title: Maratha Raids on Bengal (Bargi Invasions)
subtitle: Maratha Raids on Bengal (Bargi Invasions)
summary: Between 1741 and 1751, repeated Maratha raids, remembered in Bengal as Bargi invasions, devastated parts of Bengal and strained Alivardi Khan's regime.
heroTagline: Maratha Raids on Bengal (Bargi Invasions) reshaped power and governance patterns in Bengal.
whyItMatters: The raids matter because they exposed the fiscal and military fragility of Bengal's nawabi state and left a deep imprint on rural memory, including the folk image of the Bargi.
longTermLegacy: The Bargi raids became a lasting symbol of insecurity in eighteenth-century Bengal and helped explain why later nawabi politics operated under severe military and revenue pressure.
identityMemoryNotes: Popular memory often preserves the raids through stories of rural fear and disruption, while political history links them to the weakening of Bengal's eighteenth-century regime.

claimCitations.claim: Between 1741 and 1751, repeated Maratha raids, remembered in Bengal as Bargi invasions, devastated parts of Bengal and strained Alivardi Khan's regime.
The raids matter because they exposed the fiscal and military fragility of Bengal's nawabi state and left a deep imprint on rural memory, including the folk image of the Bargi.
The Bargi raids became a lasting symbol of insecurity in eighteenth-century Bengal and helped explain why later nawabi politics operated under severe military and revenue pressure.
Popular memory often preserves the raids through stories of rural fear and disruption, while political history links them to the weakening of Bengal's eighteenth-century regime.
